start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep my Elestio server's update times as its row says: security updates Sunday 05:00 UTC, software updates Sunday 01:00 UTC." It runs tool:keep-an-elestio-update-schedule and tells you what it changed.
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing: the schedules are the computer row's, and it makes Elestio equal them and answers what it read before and after.
instructions: 1. Read the computer's row: its Elestio account email, project and service (vm_id), and the update schedules it keeps.
2. Call tools:run with tool tool:keep-an-elestio-update-schedule and input {email, project_id, vm_id, system, app}; apply false first to see the difference. The key is the held value elestio-api-key.
3. Read sent, before and after. ok false says what still differs.

worked_examples.title: Schedules already equal to the row
worked_examples.ask: Is my Elestio server's update schedule what its row says?
worked_examples.given: Read on Nov 25 2026 against one real Elestio service (shown with made-up ids) whose panel kept OS updates on Sunday 05:00 UTC, security only, and software updates on Sunday 01:00 UTC.
